evidence: src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts: InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository implement the domain repository interfaces. UuidGenerator implements IdGenerator.

src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp() builds the repositories and passes them into UserService and TaskManagementService. Every route handler calls a service method (createProject, getProject, addTask, listTasks, assignTask, markDone) and none accesses a repository directly.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: one error middleware maps ValidationError to 400, NotFoundError to 404 and ConflictError to 409, and this mapping is not repeated anywhere else.
src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts: InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject is the only place that filters tasks by status and assigneeId. app.ts only forwards the query values through str().

src/infrastructure/app.ts: the PUT /tasks/:taskId/assignee handler checks `typeof assigneeId !== "string" || assigneeId === ""` itself. The other handlers leave validation to the service, so this is an inconsistency, but it can't be confirmed as a duplicate without the service source.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only calls createApp().listen(port); this is a thin entrypoint.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files form one infrastructure adapter concern. inMemoryRepositories.ts provides the persistence adapters and the ID adapter. app.ts wires those adapters into the application services and exposes them over HTTP. It also translates domain errors into status codes, and that mapping lives only in the error middleware. server.ts is a thin entrypoint that starts the app. Every route goes through UserService or TaskManagementService and never touches a repository directly, so no handler bypasses the module's abstractions. Task filtering by status and assignee is implemented once, in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject, and app.ts only forwards the query values. There are two small issues, and neither is clearly a failure. First, the PUT /tasks/:taskId/assignee handler checks assigneeId itself and throws ValidationError, while the other handlers pass raw input to the service to validate. That breaks the pattern and may repeat a check that belongs in the application layer, but the service source isn't available to confirm a duplicate. Second, UuidGenerator sits in a file named for in-memory repositories, which is a naming mismatch, not a split into unrelated concerns.
